A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEAM benchmark and LIGHT framework. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison of methods, equations, results, figures, and tables; minor layout defects do not prevent reliable interpretation.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-model BEAM evaluations, component ablations, retrieval experiments, and human conversation-quality ratings.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds embedding/index experiments, ReadAgent results, annotator-agreement measurements, and qualitative error analysis.

M1.justification: BEAM generation and LIGHT's episodic retrieval, working memory, scratchpad construction/compression, and filtering procedures remain unchanged. Alternative embeddings and indexes appear in sensitivity experiments. The algorithms and all 44 prompt listings are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same BEAM coverage: 100 conversations across 19 domains, 2,000 probing questions, ten memory abilities, and conversation lengths spanning approximately 100K–10M tokens. The added experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.5 and Table 13 add ReadAgent as an evaluated memory-method comparator. The existing long-context LLM, RAG, and dense-versus-SPLADE comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New experiments compare bge-small with bge-large embeddings and IndexFlatIP with IndexHNSWFlat, holding the reader at GPT-4.1-nano. Existing scoring metrics, inference settings, and retrieval-budget grids remain unchanged. Expanded annotation instructions document the existing evaluation rather than establish a changed procedure.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3–C.4 add controlled tests of embedding-model and index sensitivity. New Appendix G reports manual failure analysis across all ten memory abilities, distinguishing missing evidence from failures to use available evidence. Existing component and retrieval analyses also receive revised results and conclusions.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly reports Cohen's kappa from two annotators independently assessing 20 conversations: 0.7044 for coherence, 0.7391 for realism, and 0.7849 for complexity. v1 reports no agreement estimates. This disclosure does not establish additional experimental runs; model-result uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Table 1 is unchanged, but Tables 8–10 revise the 100K/500K base averages from 0.308/0.326 to 0.311/0.316. At 500K, SPLADE's unchanged 0.323 consequently exceeds the revised dense score. Tables 11–13 add substantial embedding, indexing, and ReadAgent results, while Appendix G adds qualitative failure findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, LIGHT memory definitions, and evaluation reasoning are retained. No substantive definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: coherent conversations up to 10M tokens, BEAM's broad memory evaluation, LIGHT's three memory components, and the claimed 3.5%–12.69% average improvement. Added studies extend support for these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G substantially expands the limitations discussion, attributing failures to incomplete retrieval, confusion between similar facts, lost chronology, position/frequency bias, and reasoning errors despite available evidence. Appendix C.3 adds an embedding-robustness interpretation. Section 4.2 also revises the working-memory and retrieval interpretations following corrected appendix values.

D1.justification: v2 discloses annotator expertise, training/calibration, and sampling of beginning, middle, ending, and random dialogue turns. It explicitly identifies Qwen2.5-32B-AWQ for ablations and IndexFlatIP for the original indexing setup, and specifies configurations for the new sensitivity tests. The repository link and prompt collection are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds MemoryCode, ReadAgent, and Kalai et al.'s hallucination paper. These support a limited expansion of benchmark positioning, an additional memory-method comparison, and failure interpretation; the broader relationship to prior research remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. Changes include explicit links between generation stages and Figure 1, expanded annotation explanations, additional appendix subsections, localized wording corrections, and publication/acknowledgment updates. The unchanged prompt appendix moves from G to H.

P2.justification: Tables 11–13 add displays using the established table format. Figures 3–5 are updated, Figure 4 is enlarged, and captions for Figures 1–4 expand. These are localized presentation changes; reflow also introduces a page-number overlap within Table 10 on v2 page 32.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through annotation procedures and agreement estimates, aligns appendix base results with Table 1, and adds useful sensitivity, baseline, and failure evidence. These strengthen the paper modestly. ReadAgent settings and error-analysis sampling remain insufficiently specified, and the new Table 10 footer overlap slightly harms readability.
